No, that's not right, and it matters for your design. A language model doesn't remember earlier conversations on its own. The assistant won't recall what a student said last week unless your code saves it and gives it back.

It's tempting to think otherwise because a chat app feels continuous. The model is more like a car with no trip computer and no odometer memory. Each call starts cold, and it only knows what's in the text you send that time. The app does the remembering. It keeps the conversation and resends all of it with each new message. Once a conversation ends, nothing is left unless you stored it.

For the makerspace assistant, that means:

- Within one session, your code resends the earlier turns each time, so the model appears to remember.
- Between sessions, nothing carries over by default.
- To remember a student's training status, you save it yourself (a file or database row per student).
- At the start of the next visit, you load the relevant facts and put them in the context.

This is the design choice in your mission: what the assistant keeps in its context versus what it saves between visits. It also affects cost. Everything you put back in is text you pay for on every call.

Quick check: a student says "I finished the laser cutter training" on Monday and returns Friday. In your own words, what has to happen for the assistant to know that on Friday?

If you want, I can build a short hands-on lesson where you see this by calling a model twice, with and without the saved history.
